Text:
One single continuous photograph — no panels, grids, or split frames.
A photorealistic 1985 photograph of a wide single-storey electronics superstore with a flat roof, plain grey panelled walls, a tall tapered entry tower at the corner of the frontage, a curved canopy wrapping the entrance beneath it, and a broad asphalt parking lot in front of the entrance, shot from the parking lot towards the entrance.
Use the uploaded photo as the exact base composition. It shows this same place in an earlier year: first remove EVERY person, vehicle and bicycle already in it, so the lot and the frontage are bare, then populate them as specified below. Keep none of the earlier year's figures or traffic.

CONTINUITY
The same location 10 years later: same camera position, framing, building footprint, parking geometry, landscaping islands and neighbouring storefronts. Only historical content changes.

LOGO
The store name across the facade is unchanged from the uploaded photo: same sign, same place, same size. It reads "Circuit City" and is built like this:
- the wordmark CIRCUIT CITY in red block capitals across the face of the entry tower
- individual channel letters mounted directly onto the tower face, no sign box
- a red plug-and-prong element beside the wordmark
- the tower face behind the letters painted deep red
LOGO REFERENCE
Reproduce the letterforms, proportions, spacing and slant from the attached reference image. Apply them as channel letters mounted on the facade at the size and position the building already gives the sign. Use the reference for the logo only — never its background, lighting, framing or composition.

LOGO FAIL
The sign is wrong if any of these describes it:
- lettering inside a lit sign box
- the flat post-2016 wordmark of the online-only brand
- any blue or orange in the lettering or the tower
- the wordmark on the main wall instead of the tower
- script or italic letterforms

SCENE
The place reads thriving — confident, loud, boom-era retail.
The parking lot is full — nearly every bay taken, cars queuing for the ones that are not.
Neighbouring units along the same frontage: hair salon, shoe store, savings bank.

VEHICLES
The vehicles are of the period — for example downsized sedans, boxy minivans, small pickups, or anything else in keeping with the year. Nothing newer than the year of the photograph appears anywhere in frame.

PEOPLE
A steady stream of shoppers crosses the frontage, walking to and from the entrance and across the lot, each one doing something plainly ordinary.
Period clothing and grooming: bright tracksuits, padded-shoulder jackets, acid-wash denim.
Every person is a different individual — no repeated face, build, pose or outfit.

PERIOD DETAILS
Store signage reading "NO MONEY DOWN", "BIG SCREEN TV", "VCR SALE".
Period advertising and fittings: Sony, RCA, payphone panel.
Place each detail where it plausibly belongs — sidewalk, storefront, lot edge, under an overhang. If there is nowhere for one, leave it out; nothing stands in the roadway or a driving lane.
No other readable text appears anywhere in the image.

TREES
The trees in the landscaping islands and along the lot edge: clearly larger than in the uploaded photo — about 115% of its canopy there, thicker trunk.
Tree sizes MUST follow this specification even where they differ from the uploaded photo.

PHOTOGRAPHIC STYLE
COLOUR photograph — Kodacolor VR 200 or Fujicolor 100 — saturated but natural, fine grain.
Photorealistic — NOT black-and-white, no HDR.

PRIVACY
Blur every face and make every licence plate unreadable.
